dedupe_keys.name: usgs global vs30 site condition map and us vs30 compilation

description: The USGS Vs30 pages provide maps of the time-averaged shear-wave velocity in the top 30 metres of ground, the main site parameter used to amplify earthquake shaking in hazard and loss models. The global hybrid Vs30 mosaic (Heath and others, 2020) is given at 30 arc-second resolution between latitudes 56 degrees south and 84 degrees north, with values from 98 to 2197 metres per second; it is offered as a GMT grid file of about 631 MB and in a map application. A separate compilation gives measured Vs30 at 2,997 sites in the United States. The data are produced by the USGS and are available free; USGS data are in the public domain. Caveats: proxy-based values carry large uncertainty at any single site and should be replaced by local measurements for design. It supplies the site-amplification layer for ShakeMap-style scenario and probabilistic seismic analyses of infrastructure networks; a related record is the USGS National Seismic Hazard Model.
